newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan businessmen among hostages in Lima - reports.
newsitem.headline: Japan businessmen among hostages in Lima - reports.

text.p: Scores of business executives from big Japanese companies as well as diplomats and Peruvian politicians are among the 200 or more hostages being held by guerrillas at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru, Japanese media reports said on Wednesday.

Besides Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, Agriculture Minister Rodolfo Munante Sanguineti and Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki, the heavily armed group took many Japanese businessmen hostage, Japan's public NHK television and Kyodo news agency said.

Among those held hostage were executives from the Lima branches of Toyota Motor Corp, NEC Corp, Asahi Chemical Industry Co, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co and Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, NHK said.
Kyodo news agency said businessmen from trading firms Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd were also among those held prisoner.

Other hostages include dozens of Japanese-Peruvians and members of various provincial associations including the Peru-Okinawa Association, Japanese students in Peru and members of a Japanese Catholic association, NHK added.
The hostages were attending a reception hosted by ambassador Morihisa Aoki to celebrate Emperor Akihito's 63rd birthday when the guerrillas attacked the residence.
The guerrillas have threatened to kill the hostages unless the Peruvian government freed imprisoned fellow rebels.
